lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: renewals, expiries, and advance reminders

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic renewals, expiries, and advance reminders task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Working with three fictional renewal-type items and invented dates (for example, a made-up membership, a made-up permit-like renewal, and a made-up subscription), the learner sets an advance reminder, a mid-point check, and a final deadline reminder for each, then explains the spacing logic they used.
safetyNotes: All renewal items and dates in this practice are invented; no real account, subscription, or document renewal date is required.
materials: learner-local: paper or a calendar/notes app
learner-local: the three provided fictional renewal-item prompts

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Of the three tiers, which one do you think you would be most likely to ignore in real life, and why?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u01-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Ladder structure: Every item has three genuinely distinct, staggered reminder dates in the correct order. | Transfer reasoning: The reflection names a specific tier and gives a plausible reason it would be the one ignored. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner design a fourth tier for a renewal item with real consequences for missing it entirely (not just inconvenience), and explain what changes about the reminder ladder when the stakes are higher.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic renewals, expiries, and advance reminders task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: the three provided fictional renewal-item prompts

resources.title: renewals, expiries, and advance reminders worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Working with three fictional renewal-type items and invented dates (for example, a made-up membership, a made-up permit-like renewal, and a made-up subscription), the learner sets an advance reminder, a mid-point check, and a final deadline reminder for each, then explains the spacing logic they used.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact renewals, expiries, and advance reminders decision or action.
Model move 2: Before building the ladder, think about a time a deadline snuck up on you.
Model move 3: For the first fictional renewal item, set an advance, mid, and final reminder with invented dates.

Model check: Ladder structure: Every item has three genuinely distinct, staggered reminder dates in the correct order. | Transfer reasoning: The reflection names a specific tier and gives a plausible reason it would be the one ignored.

resources.title: renewals, expiries, and advance reminders action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for renewals, expiries, and advance reminders.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: renewals, expiries, and advance reminders coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Working with three fictional renewal-type items and invented dates (for example, a made-up membership, a made-up permit-like renewal, and a made-up subscription), the learner sets an advance reminder, a mid-point check, and a final deadline reminder for each, then explains the spacing logic they used.
Coach direction: Before building the ladder, think about a time a deadline snuck up on you.
Learner prompt: Think of any deadline (school or otherwise) that snuck up on you before. What would an earlier reminder have needed to look like to actually help?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: renewals, expiries, and advance reminders complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For the first fictional renewal item, set an advance, mid, and final reminder with invented dates.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I set an advance reminder well before the invented deadline.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I set a mid-point check-in reminder.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I set a final reminder close to the invented deadline.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: renewals, expiries, and advance reminders minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Of the three tiers, which one do you think you would be most likely to ignore in real life, and why?

Success checks: Ladder structure: Every item has three genuinely distinct, staggered reminder dates in the correct order. | Transfer reasoning: The reflection names a specific tier and gives a plausible reason it would be the one ignored.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: renewals, expiries, and advance reminders supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u01-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional renewals, expiries, and advance reminders condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Ladder structure: Every item has three genuinely distinct, staggered reminder dates in the correct order. | Transfer reasoning: The reflection names a specific tier and gives a plausible reason it would be the one ignored..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
